concepts.name: Managed Host
concepts.definition: A host whose lifecycle NICo manages, made up of the x86/ARM host with its GPUs, zero or more DPUs, the host BMC, and the DPU BMCs.

concepts.name: Data Processing Unit (DPU)
concepts.definition: A programmable network card (NVIDIA BlueField) plugged into a host. It runs its own OS and NICo agents and handles that host's networking.

concepts.name: DPU mode vs NIC mode
concepts.definition: BlueField devices can run as a full DPU that NICo manages, or as a plain NIC. Changing mode takes a host power cycle, and devices in NIC mode are not attached as managed DPUs.

concepts.name: Baseboard Management Controller (BMC)
concepts.definition: A separate controller on a server board that manages the server out-of-band (power, boot settings, sensors, firmware), whether or not the main OS is running.

concepts.name: Redfish API
concepts.definition: A DMTF standard REST/HTTPS API that BMCs expose for inventory, power control, BIOS settings, boot order and sensors. Its resources sit under /redfish/v1.

concepts.name: libredfish and nv-redfish
concepts.definition: The two Rust Redfish client libraries NICo uses. libredfish has vendor-specific implementations. nv-redfish generates typed code from the Redfish schema and is gradually replacing libredfish.

concepts.name: gRPC
concepts.definition: A remote procedure call framework that runs over HTTP/2 and uses protobuf. NICo Core, RMS and Flow expose their APIs over gRPC.

concepts.name: NICo Core
concepts.definition: The central NICo control plane binary. It serves the gRPC API, runs the state machines for all managed resources, and is the only component that talks to the PostgreSQL database.

concepts.name: NICo REST API
concepts.definition: The REST service in front of NICo, used for tenant- and org-level operations such as per-org identity config. It runs Temporal workflows.

concepts.name: NICo state machines
concepts.definition: Idempotent state-handling functions that move resources (hosts, network segments, IB and NVLink partitions) from their actual state toward the desired state. API handlers only set the desired state.

concepts.name: Desired vs actual state reconciliation
concepts.definition: A control pattern where requests record what should be true and background loops keep acting until the real system matches it.

concepts.name: Site Explorer
concepts.definition: A background module in NICo Core. It keeps crawling BMCs over Redfish, records inventory, pairs hosts with their DPUs, and starts ingestion once a host is ready.

concepts.name: Expected Machines manifest
concepts.definition: A list of the machines a NICo site should manage, with their BMC MAC addresses, factory default passwords and optional DPU serials. Site Explorer needs it to work.

concepts.name: DPU-host pairing
concepts.definition: Site Explorer works out which DPU belongs to which host by matching the serial numbers reported by host and DPU BMCs, then checks DPU mode and completeness.

concepts.name: Host ingestion
concepts.definition: The process of bringing a discovered host under NICo management. It starts once all of the host's components are found, paired and on acceptable firmware.

concepts.name: Preingestion Manager
concepts.definition: A Core module that updates firmware, runs resets and recovers DPU BFB images on hosts that are too old to be ingested normally.

concepts.name: Machine Update Manager
concepts.definition: A Core scheduler that picks hosts and DPUs with outdated firmware for automatic updates. The ManagedHost state machine then carries out the updates.

concepts.name: DHCP
concepts.definition: The protocol that devices use to get IP addresses and network settings automatically. Relays forward requests from other network segments to the server.

concepts.name: nico-dhcp and Kea hook
concepts.definition: NICo's central DHCP service, built as a Kea DHCP server hook. It is a stateless proxy that turns DHCP requests into gRPC discover_dhcp calls to Core, which assigns the IP addresses.

concepts.name: Underlay and HostInband network segments
concepts.definition: NICo's physical network segment types. Underlay carries BMC and DPU out-of-band interfaces. HostInband is shared by zero-DPU host OS interfaces and, optionally, their BMCs.

concepts.name: PXE / iPXE network boot
concepts.definition: Booting a machine over the network instead of from a local disk. nico-pxe serves iPXE scripts, user-data and OS images over HTTP, for example nico.efi for DPUs and scout.efi for hosts.

concepts.name: UEFI boot order and BIOS settings
concepts.definition: Firmware settings that decide which device a machine boots from and which platform features (such as SR-IOV) are on. NICo sets them through Redfish.

concepts.name: cloud-init
concepts.definition: A standard tool that configures a machine on first boot from supplied user-data. NICo uses it to pass the machine_id and API endpoint to a booting DPU.

concepts.name: Scout
concepts.definition: A NICo agent that runs on hosts and DPUs. It collects inventory, runs cleanup when an instance is released, runs validation tests, and does health checks.

concepts.name: DPU Agent
concepts.definition: A NICo daemon on each managed DPU. It configures the DPU, runs health checks, configures the local DHCP server, serves the metadata service, and updates itself.

concepts.name: Instance metadata service (IMDS / FMDS)
concepts.definition: An HTTP API, served by the DPU agent, that workloads on a bare-metal instance call to learn about their instance (such as Machine ID) and to get identity tokens.

concepts.name: Bare-metal instance and tenant
concepts.definition: A tenant (an organization) is given a managed host as a bare-metal instance to run its workloads. When the instance is released, the host is cleaned and reused.

concepts.name: nico-hw-health
concepts.definition: A service that polls every host and DPU BMC over Redfish for sensors, firmware and logs. It exports Prometheus metrics and sends health reports to Core.

concepts.name: Prometheus metrics
concepts.definition: A pull-based monitoring system. Services expose numeric metrics over HTTP, and Prometheus scrapes and stores them.

concepts.name: ssh-console
concepts.definition: A NICo service that gives tenants and admins virtual serial console access to hosts through their BMCs, and sends console output to Loki.

concepts.name: nico-dns and Unbound
concepts.definition: NICo's DNS setup. nico-dns is authoritative for NICo zones. The Unbound recursive resolver answers managed machines and forwards NICo zone queries to nico-dns.

concepts.name: InfiniBand partitions and UFM
concepts.definition: InfiniBand networks are split into partitions identified by pkeys, managed by NVIDIA's UFM fabric manager. NICo's IB Fabric Monitor uses UFM to bind host ports to the right partitions.

concepts.name: NVLink partitions and NMX-C
concepts.definition: NVLink logical partitions group GPUs across a multi-node NVLink domain. NICo's NVLink Manager keeps them in line with the NMX-C controller.

concepts.name: Kubernetes
concepts.definition: The container orchestration platform that runs the NICo control plane. NICo uses its Deployments, StatefulSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets and namespaces.

concepts.name: Helm charts and values
concepts.definition: Helm packages Kubernetes manifests into charts, configured through values files. NICo and its prerequisites are installed this way.

concepts.name: NICo site config (TOML)
concepts.definition: The TOML configuration file nico-api reads at startup, with sections such as [machine_identity], [secrets] and [rms]. Invalid sections can stop the API from starting.

concepts.name: Day 0 vs Day 1 configuration
concepts.definition: Day 0 is the site-wide setup done once at bring-up. Day 1 is the later per-tenant or per-org configuration built on top of it.

concepts.name: PostgreSQL
concepts.definition: The relational database that stores NICo state (nicodb). RMS and Flow use it as well, each with its own database.

concepts.name: HashiCorp Vault
concepts.definition: A secrets management server. NICo uses it by default to store credentials (KV) and to issue certificates. Its Transit engine can also hold encryption keys.

concepts.name: Envelope encryption and KEK
concepts.definition: Data is encrypted with data keys, and those keys are in turn encrypted (wrapped) with a master key encryption key (KEK). You keep the KEK safe and track its key ID so you can rotate it.

concepts.name: AES-GCM symmetric encryption
concepts.definition: An authenticated symmetric cipher that uses a shared secret key (here 256-bit) to provide both confidentiality and integrity. Additional authenticated data (AAD) binds extra context into the ciphertext.

concepts.name: NICo credential store (secrets backends)
concepts.definition: The way NICo stores BMC, UEFI and switch credentials. Vault is the default, or credentials can be kept encrypted per row in Postgres under a KEK from an Integrated, Transit or KMIP provider.

concepts.name: Factory default credentials
concepts.definition: The vendor default BMC and UEFI passwords that NICo needs to log into new hardware for the first time. They can be seeded into Vault, imported, or added through the CLI.

concepts.name: TLS certificates and mutual TLS
concepts.definition: TLS encrypts connections using certificates signed by a certificate authority (CA). With mutual TLS, both client and server present certificates and verify each other.

concepts.name: cert-manager and ClusterIssuer
concepts.definition: cert-manager is a Kubernetes add-on that issues certificates. A ClusterIssuer is the cluster-wide signer it uses, backed by either Vault or a local site CA.

concepts.name: SPIFFE
concepts.definition: A standard for workload identity. Workloads get a SPIFFE ID within a trust domain and prove it with an SVID, which is either an X.509 certificate or a JWT.

concepts.name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
concepts.definition: A signed, compact token that carries claims such as issuer, audience and expiry. Verifiers check its signature against the issuer's published keys (JWKS).

concepts.name: Machine identity (JWT-SVID issuance)
concepts.definition: A NICo feature that signs short-lived SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs for workloads on instances, through the Core gRPC API or IMDS. Each org has its own signing keys, which are encrypted under the site KEK.

concepts.name: Token delegation (RFC 8693 token exchange)
concepts.definition: An OAuth standard for exchanging one token for another at a security token service (STS). NICo can use it to delegate tokens to external STS endpoints, optionally through an egress proxy.

concepts.name: Rate limiting (GCRA token bucket)
concepts.definition: An algorithm that caps the sustained request rate and allows short bursts. The DPU agent uses it for IMDS identity requests.

concepts.name: Temporal workflows
concepts.definition: A durable workflow engine that keeps the state of long-running, multi-step operations so they survive restarts. Flow and nico-rest use it.

concepts.name: NICo Flow
concepts.definition: A service that tracks rack inventory and runs durable rack-level tasks (power, firmware, ingestion, bring-up). Each task follows an operation rule's ordered stages and runs on Temporal.

concepts.name: Component Manager
concepts.definition: A pluggable layer that performs hardware operations for one class of component (compute tray, switch, power shelf) through a configured backend such as RMS or direct Redfish.

concepts.name: Rack Management Service (RMS)
concepts.definition: A separate NVIDIA service that NICo calls over mTLS gRPC to carry out rack-level hardware operations. It speaks Redfish, NVUE, SSH/SFTP and gNMI to the devices.

concepts.name: NVL rack components
concepts.definition: The hardware in an NVIDIA NVL rack: compute trays, NVSwitch trays (which run NVOS and are managed through NVUE), and power shelves.

concepts.name: Firmware manifest and rack profile
concepts.definition: A rack profile points to a JSON firmware manifest listing firmware components and artifact URLs. NICo forwards the manifest to RMS, and RMS downloads the artifacts itself.

concepts.name: Asynchronous job polling
concepts.definition: A pattern where a request returns a job ID right away, and the caller polls a status API until the job reaches completed or failed.

concepts.name: Loki logging
concepts.definition: A log aggregation system queried through Grafana or logcli. It stores logs from control-plane components and host serial consoles.

concepts.name: Power control reset types
concepts.definition: The Redfish reset actions used to power-cycle hosts and DPUs. They range from a graceful restart to a full AC power cycle.
